q: My buyer wants a third-party verified carbon footprint. What does that involve for a small supplier?
title: Third-party verified footprint
short: First build a documented inventory or product footprint, then hire an accredited body to verify it: ISO 14064-3 for a company inventory, or a critical review or verification for an ISO 14067 product footprint. Verifiers sample invoices, so records matter more than reports.
audience: MSME suppliers asked for verified emissions data

ol: Agree with the buyer: company inventory or product footprint, and which year.
Collect fuel, electricity and production records for that period.
Prepare the calculation with factors and sources.
Engage a verifier and answer their sample requests.

p: Some buyers accept a documented calculation for the first year. Check before paying for verification.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and production documents into dated, fingerprinted plant records, so the monthly intensity behind a compliance figure can be traced to its source.
